scope: Official mechanism documentation supporting a proposed deployment mapping; no SQLite adapter or complete multi-device protocol was implemented in this revision.

checked_claims: The specification permits both per-user and per-device identity keys.
Application retransmission can use a new active session and is not necessarily the paper's exact replay.

locations: Keeping message history and other application states in sync across devices
checked_claims: The documented one-to-one design uses pairwise encrypted sessions and client fanout.
Group Sender Key operation is separately described.
Message history and application-state synchronization are separately described.

locations: 3 Response To Errors Within A Transaction
checked_claims: SQLite permits one simultaneous local write transaction.
Error handling must inspect actual transaction state rather than equate every error with a wholly absent transaction.
WAL FULL adds a synchronization for each committed transaction.
WAL NORMAL may lose committed transactions after system crash or power loss, while committed transactions remain durable across application crashes.
A WAL commit does not require a prior checkpoint into the main database.
WAL is persistent database state; copying only the main database can omit it.
WAL does not provide atomic commit across multiple attached databases as a group or distributed device synchronization.
WAL frames may have been written before their transaction commits.
sources.inference_from_paper: An intact recoverable version retained in those frames belongs to the acquisition history at its first durable retention; a later logical rollback does not erase an already acquired copy. This does not identify every incomplete frame with Saved(v).

checked_claims: SQLCipher encrypts individual database pages and authenticates encrypted page data.
Page data in WAL files is encrypted with the database key.
sources.inference_from_mechanism: Page encryption and authentication alone do not establish the protocol's ownership, rollback freshness, or multi-device synchronization contract.

checked_claims: WCDB is based on SQLite and SQLCipher and exposes SQLCipher encryption support.
